correctness.rationale: The formal derivative is exact for even N; termwise integration yields a convergent p-adic series. The leading j=1 term has valuation N+alpha+2. Identity (2) and case-separated bounds for every j>=2 prove all other terms have valuation at least N+alpha+3. The strong non-Archimedean triangle inequality then proves the exact value for all odd primes, p-units a, alpha>=1. The standalone Fraction checker reproduces 68 finite cases; finite checks are not a substitute for the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: Farhi singles out n=2p^alpha-1 as the exact lower-bound indices; finding the p-adic valuation at their immediate successor is a natural structural question. The theorem gives a sharp, uniform and unexpected spike and exact adjacent difference 2alpha+2 for every odd prime and every p-adic unit parameter. This is a meaningful local exactness result for a natural rational sequence, not an arbitrary finite computation.
